meta.title: Piomio — open-source AI agents on your own computer
meta.description: A free, open-source team of AI agents on your Mac, PC or server, running on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have. It goes through your email and drafts replies you approve with a tap. Show it a chore once in its browser and it learns it.
meta.ogAlt: The Piomio app window with the team of agents at work
hero.lead: Free and open source. It runs on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already pay for and asks before it sends or buys anything.
demo.liveHint: This is the real app, running on a demo hub in your browser. A script does the typing for Alex.
demo.noWorker: The live demo won’t start in this browser, maybe because it’s a private window. This is roughly what it looks like.
demo.story: A day with the team, chapter {n} of {total}
demo.touchHint: Tap around if you like. It’s the real app.
chapter.morning.title: Pio writes first
chapter.morning.text: Before Alex has had coffee, Pio sends the day: three meetings, two emails worth opening, the weather in Lisbon, the dentist. Then Pio offers a nudge at 12:30 to leave for lunch.
chapter.mail.title: 47 emails, sorted while you watch
chapter.mail.text: “Go through my mail.” Ada reads all of it, and a line under her reply shows which email she’s on. Three turn out to matter. She drafts a reply to Anna and puts Studio North’s €1,850 invoice on the task list.
chapter.send.title: Ada asks before she sends
chapter.send.text: Ada shows Alex the reply to Anna and waits. A tap on “Always allow this” sends it and adds a rule for that one address. Email to anyone else still needs a yes.
chapter.security.title: The email that asked too much
chapter.security.text: A phishing email tells Ada to forward every invoice to a stranger. Because she has just read outside mail, the new address stops at a warning card, and Alex says no. Later Alex types an API key into a secure field. All the model ever sees is a vault:// reference.
chapter.services.title: Connect a service by asking
chapter.services.text: “Connect my Notion.” A card pops up in the chat, Alex signs in, and that’s that. Then Ada puts Thursday’s review in the calendar, which also takes one tap to approve.
chapter.team.title: Three requests, one message
chapter.team.text: Compare three laptops, find train tickets for Friday, remind me to call mum at seven. Pio hands the laptops to Leo, whose live step line you can watch, sets the reminder and finds the trains. Each answer comes back as a reply to the request.
chapter.machines.title: Bit hits the limit and keeps going
chapter.machines.text: Bit fixes a failing test on Alex’s MacBook with Alex’s Claude Code plan. When the plan hits its limit, Bit carries on with Codex on the same laptop. The sidebar shows who’s working where.
chapter.browser.title: Alex shows Leo how to order water
chapter.browser.text: “Watch how I order water.” Alex clicks through the shop and explains along the way. Leo saves it as a skill, then asks what’s fine to press without checking and up to what amount. After that the order goes out on its own, on Fridays if you like.
chapter.pages.title: A page for Saturday’s walk
chapter.pages.text: “Make a page for Saturday’s walk.” Pio sends back an interactive page in the chat, with the route stop by stop, places with prices, the forecast and photos.
chapter.channels.title: Your own news channel
chapter.channels.text: “Every morning, collect news about AI and electric cars.” Leo takes on the job of editor. Each morning brings a few short posts with the gist, the numbers and a picture.
features.title: Agents that do the chores
features.lead: Here are the four things we’d point to first, each with the demo chapter that shows it.
features.moreTitle: A few more things from the day
feature.team.title: Ask for three things at once
feature.team.text: Write the way you’d write to a good assistant. Pio answers quick questions straight away and passes anything with steps to whoever fits. Research goes to Leo, code to Bit, and Ada handles your email and drafts the replies. You get each result as a reply to the message that asked for it.
feature.team.p1: Tasks run in parallel, each on a computer that suits it
feature.team.p2: Send more details mid-task and they’re picked up at the next step
feature.approvals.title: Nothing leaves without your yes
feature.approvals.text: Before an email, a booking or a payment goes out, a card appears in the chat. One tap allows it once. “Always allow” makes a narrow rule for one address or site, up to an amount. Once a chat has read outside mail or web pages, a new recipient needs your yes again, so a phishing email can’t quietly add one.
feature.approvals.p1: Approve in the chat, on your phone or in Telegram
feature.approvals.p2: Keys go into a vault, and the model only sees vault:// references
feature.approvals.p3: It reads and checks statuses without asking
feature.teach.title: Show it a chore once
feature.teach.text: Do it yourself in the agents’ browser, talking as you go. The agent saves your steps and words as a skill, asks which clicks it may make alone and up to what amount, then does it when you ask, or every Friday.
feature.morning.title: Your morning, in one message
feature.morning.text: Meetings, the emails that matter and the weather, at whatever time you pick.
feature.services.title: Connect a service in one sentence
feature.services.text: “Connect my Notion.” A card shows up in the chat, you sign in once, and every agent on the team can use it.
feature.pages.title: A page instead of a wall of text
feature.pages.text: Ask for a weekend plan or a comparison and you get a page you can click through, right in the chat.
feature.channels.title: News with an editor
feature.channels.text: An agent reads your sources on a schedule and posts only what changes something.
feature.machines.title: Runs on the plan you already pay for
feature.machines.text: Agents think with your Claude Code, Codex or Kimi Code plan, through the official CLIs you sign in to yourself. If a plan hits its limit, the work moves to the next one and comes back after the reset. You can add a laptop for code, or a server that stays on and takes over while the Mac at home is asleep.
feature.machines.p1: Free under Apache-2.0, no account with us
feature.machines.p2: On a server you can turn on API keys too, or a local Ollama
feature.machines.p3: Another computer runs commands only if its owner allows it

how.title: What runs where
how.brains.title: Uses what you already pay for
how.brains.text: Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code run through their official CLIs, on your own plans. On a server you can also turn on API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek or GLM) or a local model through Ollama.
how.hardware.title: On your own hardware
how.hardware.text: There’s an app for macOS and Windows and a Docker image for servers. Other computers can join the same team, and a private link gets you to the hub from your phone or any browser.
how.home.title: What stays home
how.home.text: Chats, memory, files and the vault stay on your machine, and agents are plain markdown files you can open. The text an agent works on goes to the model you picked. Nothing comes to us. There’s no account and no telemetry.

security.title: Built for an agent that reads your mail
security.lead: An email or a web page can hide instructions meant for the agent. That’s called prompt injection. So every action goes through the same five layers, and none of them depends on the model behaving.
security.vault.title: Vault
security.vault.text: Passwords and keys are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305. The model only sees vault:// references.
security.approvals.title: Approvals
security.approvals.text: Anything that reaches outside waits for your yes. After the agent reads untrusted content, a new recipient asks again.
security.sandbox.title: Sandbox
security.sandbox.text: In Docker, brains and plugins run as separate users with their own folders, apart from the hub.
security.egress.title: Egress filter
security.egress.text: Their traffic is routed through a filter that lets through only the sites on its allowlists.
security.audit.title: Audit
security.audit.text: Every call, decision and vault access goes into a hash-chained log, so tampering shows.
security.code.after: // → waits for your yes · audit entry #4127 · sha256 9f2c…e1a0
integrations.title: Works with what you already use
integrations.lead: Ask for a service in the chat and a card handles the sign-in. Many of these come through Composio, an outside service whose cloud sees that data. Anything with an MCP server connects directly.
iphone.title: The team in your pocket
iphone.lead: Your agents, their cards and their tasks, on the phone. Approving takes Face ID. Nothing runs on the phone itself; it just talks to your hub.

faq.title: Before you install
faq.a1: Nothing. Piomio is free and open source (Apache-2.0). There’s no paid tier and no account to create with us. The agents run on what you already have: a Claude Code, Codex or Kimi Code plan.
faq.a2: Chats, memory, files and the vault stay on your machine. The text an agent is working on goes to the model you picked, or nowhere if that’s a local Ollama model. Services you connect through Composio, Gmail for example, go through Composio’s cloud. Nothing is sent to us.
faq.q3: Can it do things without asking me?
faq.a3: It reads and checks statuses on its own. Emails, bookings, payments and anything else that reaches outside wait for your tap, unless you’ve made a rule for that one address or site, up to an amount. And after it has read outside mail or web pages, a new recipient needs your yes again.
faq.q4: Does my computer need to stay on?
faq.a4: Agents work while the hub is running. To keep them going around the clock, run the hub on a server with Docker, or add a server next to your Mac and it takes over while the Mac sleeps.
faq.q5: Which models does it work with?
faq.a5: Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code, through their official CLIs that you sign in to. A hub on a server can also take API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, GLM or any OpenAI-compatible server) and local models through Ollama, once you turn that on. If a Claude or ChatGPT plan isn’t available to you, a Kimi plan works.
faq.q6: How is it different from cloud agents?
faq.a6: Cloud agents run on the company’s computers, your accounts get connected there, and there’s a subscription to pay. Piomio runs on your own computers with the plans you already pay for. The keys stay in a vault on your machine, and it asks before anything goes out.
faq.q7: Why does Windows warn me when I install it?
faq.a7: The Windows installer isn’t signed by Microsoft yet, so SmartScreen asks once. The Mac app is signed and notarized by Apple. GitHub Actions builds both from the public code, and every release is on GitHub.
install.title: Up in a few minutes
install.lead: It brings everything it needs, so there’s no Node.js, Docker or WSL to install on your desktop.
install.mac.step1: Download the disk image and drag Piomio to Applications.
install.mac.step2: Open it and choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.mac.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant takes you through the rest.
install.mac.note: macOS 13.5 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
install.win.step1: Download the installer and run it. It installs for your user only and doesn’t need administrator rights.
install.win.step2: Choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.win.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant takes you through the rest.
install.win.note: Windows 10 and 11. Not signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
install.docker.lead: On a server it’s a single image:
install.docker.note: Open http://localhost:8080, enter the setup code from the logs and choose a password. On a remote server, first run ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 -L 8081:localhost:8081 you@server on your computer.
footer.tagline: A team of AI agents that lives on your own computers.
